Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we’re all aligned: 

Summary of the call:
- Use case: document search + semantic ranking for product docs and support articles; ~20M documents initially, mostly short pages (avg 120 tokens).
- Current provider: VecCloud; some vectors are precomputed (1024-d, stored as float32).
- Key success metrics: 95%+ top-3 recall on our eval set, <50ms mean retrieval latency for single-query, and cost target ~50% reduction vs current provider.

Technical notes / asks we took away:
1) Embedding dimension: we recommend 1536 for best balance between accuracy and compatibility with our reranker (we'll provide AB tests).
2) Similarity scoring: cosine similarity is preferred for normalized embeddings; we can support dot-product for unnormalized workflows.
3) Migration: incremental reindexing strategy suggested (re-embed hot docs first).
4) Batching / throughput: initial batches of 64 for bulk re-embedding, SDK parallelism using our async client.
5) Auth & routing: API keys for PoC, then mutual TLS or token-based routing for Dedicated/Private.

Proposed next steps:
- Dev: Dev and Samir to sync on migration plan & initial test dataset (Mar 12).
- Marissa/Nikhil: schedule technical kickoff + SOW review (Mar 13).
- Redwood: provide SDK quickstart, sample reindex script, and suggested hyperparams (attached draft).

Attachments: call recording (acme-call-recording.mp3), draft quickstart (will attach updated version).

If that aligns, I’ll schedule the kickoff for Friday (Mar 13).

Best,
Marissa

Thanks Marissa — adding more concrete engineering guidance so ACME's team can evaluate and plan timing.

SDK / auth / routing:
- SDK: use our python async client (redwood.embeddings.AsyncClient). Quickstart attached will have examples for streaming and bulk.
- Auth: API key for initial PoC. For production, we support token exchange via STS and mTLS for Dedicated. We can share a sample IAM role mapping for cross-account access.
- Routing: our service can route requests by region or cost tier; config is just a route policy that pins embedding requests to the high-precision model.

Embeddings specifics:
- Recommended dimension: 1536 (this maps to our curated open models and yields better nearest-neighbor quality vs 1024 in our internal evals).
- Normalization: perform L2 normalization on vectors if you plan to use cosine similarity. Our similarity index supports both normalized (cosine) and raw dot-product search.
- Batching: for bulk re-embedding, use async batches of 64–128 items. For online generation, batch 8–32 depending on latency SLO. We recommend batching at the client and using our concurrent_workers parameter (default 8).
- Indexing: we support incremental reindexing — tag vectors with version metadata so you can rollback to VecCloud vectors if needed.

Migration tips from VecCloud:
- If you have precomputed 1024-d vectors, you have two options: 1) Keep them for a cold subset and re-embed hot docs (recommended), or 2) Re-embed everything with 1536-d for a clean migration.
- If you must compare, we can run a parallel A/B between VecCloud 1024-d and Redwood 1536-d on your eval set.
- Storage: recommend quantized float16/8 for disk to save ~2–4x space depending on your index. We’ll share quantization guidance.

Sample hyperparams (we’ll include runnable scripts in the quickstart):
- embed_dim = 1536
- batch_size = 64 (bulk), 16 (online)
- normalize = True (L2) if using cosine
- reindex_strategy = "hot-first"

I’ll attach a sample reindex script and a small benchmark we ran on a 1M doc subset. Happy to jump on a short tech call with Samir tomorrow.

—Dev

Thanks — this is super helpful. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Dimension: if we move from 1024->1536, what kind of delta should we expect on recall based on your internal results? A rough % is fine.
2) Runtime latency: for our retrieval pipeline (single-query retrieval + top-100 rerank), can you confirm the expected end-to-end p50 for a single user query (we target <50ms retrieval before rerank)?
3) Migration: we have about 20M vectors; re-embedding everything in one go is expensive. We like the hot-first approach. Can you outline an orchestration approach (jobs, checkpoints) that works with your SDK?

Also looped Samir (our infra lead) for the tech call. Samir — please let us know availability for a 30–45m sync tomorrow or Friday.

Olivia
Head of Search, ACME.ai

Olivia — quick answers while Dev prepares the detailed benchmark: 
- Delta on recall: early internal A/Bs show ~6–10% top-3 recall improvement moving 1024->1536 for similar corpuses; we'll validate on your eval set.
- Retrieval p50: with our managed index and the config Dev suggested (quantized storage + SSD-backed nearest neighbor), p50 retrieval to fetch top-100 is typically 15–30ms in us-west regions for single-query (no rerank). Reranker adds additional latency depending on model choice — we can push reranker to a lower-cost CPU tier if you want to keep cost down.

Commercial / next steps:
- I’ll send a SOW draft and migration engagement estimate (attached to the HubSpot deal). For PoC, we can cover engineering hours in a trial credit to validate the hot-first strategy.
- Proposed milestone: Kickoff (Mar 13) -> PoC (2–3 weeks) -> Pilot (4–8 weeks) -> Full migration (phased).
